cli_surface: Claude Code 2.1.241 --help; --print, stream-json input/output, --verbose (required with them), --replay-user-messages, --safe-mode, --no-session-persistence, and `claude setup-token` taking no options. `claude auth` offers login, logout and status, and no revoke.
distribution: a self-contained native Mach-O arm64 image. The npm package's bin entry is the platform binary itself, hard-linked from @anthropic-ai/claude-code-darwin-arm64, and it links only /usr/lib system dylibs. It is not Node-hosted, so there is no interpreter to resolve and no package tree to grant: measured against a real provider at a path answering path_not_granted, a full confined session behaves identically whether the executable's directory is granted or nothing is, because the provider's command policy grants the launched entrypoint a direct exec bypass. The same package ships a `#!/usr/bin/env node` fallback launcher for installs whose postinstall did not run, and that shape is refused by name rather than launched into a box with no interpreter declared.
argv_measured: --verbose is required, not stylistic: without it the session refuses to start with `Error: When using --print, --output-format=stream-json requires --verbose` and exits 1 having emitted nothing. --safe-mode is load-bearing in a repair box: a SessionStart hook planted in the box's own .claude/settings.json ran without the flag and did not run with it, measured both ways. The runtime's built-in skills survive the flag either way, which its own help does not say. direct_argv is the pinned part; the declared ask is appended to it as --append-system-prompt <text>, recorded under `ask`.

packet_input.text: the exact immutable packet byte sequence
packet_input.arrival_evidence: --replay-user-messages makes the runtime re-emit the message it read as a native `user` event carrying isReplay, so packet delivery is in the receipt even when the session is killed before an assistant turn exists

credential: a long-lived subscription OAuth token minted separately by `claude setup-token`; never the operator's keychain login, never an API key, and never read from the parent environment, a home directory or an auth file
credential_expiry: operator-configured: the command takes no options, prints no expiry and has no revoke, so kept refuses a dispatch that could outlive the token rather than discovering it dead mid-session
credential_channel_measured: confirmed live, without a valid token. A confined session carrying a deliberately invalid value in this variable reached api.anthropic.com through the provider's domain allowlist and the upstream answered `401 OAuth access token is invalid` in 2 seconds, naming it as an OAuth access token rather than an API key. The channel is proven this way and again with a valid one: the brokered route of docs/decision/0057 carried real repair sessions to result: success.
accepted_exposure: direct environment channel: a tool-capable agent inside the box can read CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN from its own environment, accepted explicitly under decision 0017 because the alternative on macOS is a keychain grant that decision refuses outright
child_environment: clean: HOME and CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR under a freshly-created empty directory, CLAUDE_CODE_TMPDIR naming the box's own temporary directory, plus exactly the credential environment entry; ANTHROPIC_API_KEY is refused rather than passed, as is the rest of the credential-precedence family
temporary_directory: CLAUDE_CODE_TMPDIR, and not TMPDIR. The installed binary's tmpdir resolver reads CLAUDE_CODE_TMPDIR and otherwise returns the string "/tmp", ignoring TMPDIR entirely, so a confined session without it opens /tmp/claude-<uid> — a host scratch root a repair profile denies by name — and dies with `EPERM: operation not permitted, open '/tmp/claude-501'`, exit 1, having emitted no stream event at all. The confinement profile declares the name beside the directory it grants, so the grant and the variable are one statement; a disagreement is refused before launch. See docs/decision/0056.
network: one host: api.anthropic.com, on the provider's domain allowlist. A build-only network block is wrong for this runtime and was measured as such: with the network blocked the session retried ten times with exponential backoff and gave up after 169 seconds with ConnectionRefused. Nothing else was needed to reach authentication.
native_examples_provenance: documented stream shape, hand-written to exercise every projection. It is not a recording.
captured_session_provenance: a real Claude Code 2.1.241 session, recorded verbatim from inside a confined repair box under the profile above, with the direct argv above and a deliberately invalid credential. It is evidence of the runtime's own event vocabulary, the packet's arrival, the --safe-mode surface and the credential channel's identity. It is not the interrupted live session decision 0052 requires: that one is a credentialed repair session killed at its deadline, and it lives in internal/repair/claudeadmission_test.go rather than here, because what it proves is a receipt the parent assembled rather than a stream shape.

projections.assistant.message.content[type=text].tex: transcript fragment when no streamed text arrived
projections.system: otherwise retained as a native event only; status and api_retry produce no projection
projections.user: retained as a native event only; it is the runtime's replay of the packet and never a transcript kept authored
projections.system.init.model: the model the runtime says answered; every other system subtype, and an init naming no model, project nothing
projections.rate_limit_event.rate_limit_info.unified: usage window utilization and reset, all windows or none; a window kept cannot read makes the whole reading missing rather than partial
projections.result.modelUsage: no projection: it names the model a second time, and the init already carries the one answer
projections.assistant.message.model=<synthetic>: no transcript projection: a message the runtime composed without calling a model is not something a model said. The event is retained whole and the turn is still counted, because the runtime counts it in its own num_turns

admission: admitted, on the evidence in internal/repair/claudeadmission_test.go. Three live confined sessions on 2026-08-24, Claude Code 2.1.241 under nono 0.74.0 with the operator's brokered credential against api.anthropic.com, in boxes cut from kept's own corpus and source with a promise deliberately broken there. One repaired it and the verdict was re-derived from the box's world rather than from anything the session said; one carried the packet marker and produced transcript, cost and turn projections referencing its native events; and one was killed at a fifteen-second deadline and kept its partial receipt, the timeout cause and the reaped signal, with no cost, because a session killed before its result has none. What was missing until then was not a credential and not confinement: it was that nobody had told the runtime the message was work. See `ask` above and docs/decision/0058.

brokered_credential.channel: a confinement-provider credential route, the second of the two channels decision 0052 permits and the one every live session below ran on. kept never holds the secret: the profile names a reference, the provider resolves it, publishes a session phantom in the child variable, and rewrites the phantom into the real value on egress. See docs/decision/0057.
brokered_credential.service: anthropic, because the provider publishes a route's local address as <SERVICE>_BASE_URL and this runtime already reads ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL
brokered_credential.reference: a scheme://... URI kept passes and never reads. On macOS the two that resolve are file://<absolute path> and apple-password://<server>/<account>, the latter reading the login keychain's internet password class and no other; keyring:// does not parse on this field
brokered_credential.phantom_environment_policy: published by the profile and by nothing else. An invocation naming it is refused by the launch, so the variable has one source and one policy; under this channel the adapter's child environment carries no credential at all and there is no secret in the receipt to redact
brokered_credential.endpoint_policy: default-deny at the provider, measured: an unnamed path and an unnamed method each answered 403 without reaching the upstream, and the named rule matches with a query string present
brokered_credential.child_cannot_read_the_credential: measured at a loopback listener standing in for the upstream: the child sent Bearer <phantom> and the listener received Bearer <the real value>, and the phantom is a capability rather than decoration because a wrong bearer value or none is refused at the proxy with 401 and never reaches the upstream. internal/repair/confined_test.go
brokered_credential.network: a credential route and network.block: true are refused by the provider as contradictory, and a route with no domain allowlist reaches every host, so a box with one names its host

live_sessions_measured: eleven confined sessions in total. Eight on 2026-08-23, before the declared ask, are the control and are recorded because they are what the ask was decided from: the launch half of decision 0052's table held completely — sessions started in the box, replayed the packet as a native user event, and produced native events with transcript, cost and turn projections referencing them, and two killed at a deadline retained their partial receipts beside the timeout cause and the reaped signal — while of the six that ran to their own end exactly one performed the repair, and that one had read the test authoring the break out of its own box. Every session with a clean box located the fault from the packet alone, wrote a correct account of why the promise did not hold, and stopped without editing; carrying the packet's dispatch policies changed nothing. Three on 2026-08-24, with the ask of docs/decision/0058 and nothing else changed, settled it: a session with a clean box removed the offending call and the promise re-derived from that box read kept, the diff being one line in the one file the promise's repair scope names; a second ran to its own end with 808 native events, 44 turns and 23 transcript fragments; and a third was killed at fifteen seconds holding 126 native events, 6 turn updates and no cost. internal/repair/claudeadmission_test.go
refused_parent_environment: the whole ANTHROPIC_ namespace, plus the named CLAUDE_/CLAUDE_CODE_/CCR_ and transport variables that carry a credential, name settings that can carry an auth helper, redirect where the credential is sent, or switch to a provider with its own credentials. Read off the installed 2.1.241 binary's own auth-state report and strictPolicyHelperKeys set, and re-checked name by name against 2.1.241 when the pin moved from 2.1.240. Names are consulted, never values. A third-party credential store and NO_PROXY are excluded on purpose: the provider switch is what is refused, and NO_PROXY redirects nothing

ask.channel: --append-system-prompt, appended to direct_argv above. It is a channel of its own: the packet still travels as the whole of one stdin JSONL user message with nothing prepended to it, and the ask names no promise, no file and no evidence. See docs/decision/0058.
ask.why: measured, over eight confined sessions with a live credential and a well-formed packet: the runtime located the fault exactly, wrote a correct account of why the promise did not hold, and stopped without editing. The write boundary was not the cause and carrying the packet's dispatch policies changed nothing. A packet states authority and evidence and never an ask (decision 0009), and this runtime launched with --print reads one as a question. Pi's own harness supplies this framing; Claude Code's does not.
ask.measured: the appended text is honoured under --safe-mode with --print and stream-json output, which the flag's own help does not say: --safe-mode disables what a session discovers, and an explicit argv value is not that. --system-prompt was not used because replacing the default prompt would take the runtime's own tool and permission instructions with it.
ask.not_in_the_packet: the ask is one reviewed constant per value, identical for every repair, and it is neither composed from the packet nor supplied by an operator. A channel that could carry anything could carry the per-repair instruction decision 0009 keeps out of a packet.

captured_window_provenance: the two rate_limit_event payloads from the one real repair in this repository's ledger, thread 6ca1kqeyfz205a2s4qf4cb991a on 2026-08-29, taken verbatim from the receipt's retained native events. It is a real reading of a real account: five_hour utilization moved 0.24 to 0.25 across the session and seven_day stood at 0.11. The captured_session above is the other half of the evidence and carries no rate_limit_event at all, which is what a session reporting no window looks like.
captured_synthetic_provenance: the two payloads from the one real session a runtime answered without a model: the adversarial pass over thread 4f8q0g537deca7sw2vvyvht111 on 2026-09-19, launched onto an account at its rate limit, taken verbatim from its receipt's retained native events at seq 5846 and 5849. The assistant message names model <synthetic>, carries is_api_error_message true and holds 65 bytes the runtime composed itself; the result reports is_error true, terminal_reason api_error, api_error_status 429, total_cost_usd 0 and num_turns 1. kept projected that message as the pass's transcript and filed it as the pass's argument, so the record said a pass argued when no model had answered.
